characters.name: Both
characters.description: A wacky, childish duo of sentient produce items who try to fit in as newcomers to their city. Anthropomorphic Food: A talking apple and onion. Butt-Monkey: Downplayed. While they aren’t terribly unlucky, they tend to suffer various misfortunes, ranging fromContrived Coincidencesto having to risk their lives at certain points whenever they’re focused on getting something done. Catchphrase: They usually say “Oh my days!” whenever they’re surprised. Characterization Marches On: In the pilot, they pretty much acted near identical to each other aside from the food they are and Onion’s crush on French Fry. By the time of the series proper, Apple is more foolish and absent-minded, while Onion is the more rational and snarky of the two, though they still remainCloudcuckoolanders.

characters.name: Apple
characters.description: The slightly more mellow, but very easily distracted member of the duo. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: He gets distracted easily and has trouble keeping focus. This becomes a main plot point inApple's Focus, where he tries to help Onion out with getting onto theShow Within a ShowThe Great Baking Duos, but his lack of attention ends up disrupting their practice. Catchphrase:He tends to say “It’s going to be very bum-ting!” or another variant of it whenever he approves of a plan or when things work out.Whenever someone (usually Onion) gives him a counterclaim towards his statements, he simply replies with “True.” He tends to say “It’s going to be very bum-ting!” or another variant of it whenever he approves of a plan or when things work out. Whenever someone (usually Onion) gives him a counterclaim towards his statements, he simply replies with “True.”

characters.name: Onion
characters.description: The mildly more grounded, but also incredibly neurotic member of the duo. Catchphrase: Whenever Apple is in danger or is about to do something illogical, he often says “Apple, no!” or“APPLE!” Cloudcuckoolander's Minder: Downplayed. Although he’s not above his own brand of wackiness, he tends to go into this role in regards to Apple whenever the duo ends up in a problem that requires critical thinking to get out of, where he tries to suggest more grounded solutions and opposes Apple’s usually detrimental and nonsensical plans. Furry Reminder:Onion hides from the police by sticking his head in a pot of soil and standing upside down, momentarily resembling a real spring onion.This happens again, where Onion accidentally gets his head stuck in a pot of soil in "Falafel's Fun Day". Onion hides from the police by sticking his head in a pot of soil and standing upside down, momentarily resembling a real spring onion.

characters.name: Falafel
characters.description: The put upon landlord and superintendent of Apple and Onion's building. Ascended Extra: Downplayed. While he did have an occasional episode focusing around him, his appearances would usually be minor. By Season 1’s other half, however, he would become more of a secondary character and the closest thing to a third main character besides the duo themselves. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Downplayed. While he tends to be annoyed by the duo on a frequent basis, there are many occasions where he shows that he does genuinely consider them his friends in spite of this. Butt-Monkey: Is often the unwitting victim of Apple and Onion's antics and tends to have bad luck even when they aren’t around. The Chessmaster:Played for Laughs.In the episodeWin It or Bin It, it turns out that he was the one behind everything the duo went through in order to get their luxury apartment.Yes, that even includes the eagle and the cloud.

characters.name: Hot Dog
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: He’s had two episodes focusing around him. The first beingHot Dog’s Movie Premiere, where he invites his friends to watch a movie he played in while Apple and Onion try to get past Chicken Nugget, and the second being “Nothing Can Stop Us,” where he does an acting audition, but also forgets his toupee, prompting Apple and Onion to retrieve it. Butt-Monkey: Downplayed, since he isn’t often put in this role and his misfortune is usually rather tame, but he tends to be the one who gets the low end of the stick more than the other members of his friend group. Whether that being annoyed by an obnoxious ketchup bottle at his own movie premiere, getting rejected from an audition due to being bald,and breaking his spine when trying to carry a fridge down.

characters.name: French Fry
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: The main plot of the episodeFace Your Fearshas her try to overcome her fear of public speaking by inviting Apple and Onion over to her reading of the poem she just wrote.

characters.name: Burger
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: He plays the role of the antagonist inAppleoni, where he witnesses Apple and Onion doing the titular dance they invented and ends up doing it himself, in which he takes the credit for it when he goes on TV. Big Eater: Compared to the others in the friend group he’s in, he’s the one who eats the most out of them. Lampshaded in “Not Funny” when Apple cracks a joke about him eating like a pig.

characters.name: Cotton Candy
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: She plays a major role inNot Funny, where Onion bonds more with her and inadvertently makes Apple think that he’s replacing him with her as his new best friend. Non-Standard Character Design: Compared to most of the other characters, who have human traits but still look like regular food items, she looks more explicitly human. Sassy Black Woman: Since she's a piece of cotton candy, she can be quite sassy.

characters.name: "Beej" (Beef Jerky)
characters.description: A prisoner who befriends the duo. Desires Prison Life: He once stated in an episode that he actually lives in the prison he's in, to the point where instead of leaving when the wall behind him is broken, he opts to fix it instead. Face of a Thug: Despite looking very intimidating, he’s a very nice prisoner who helps Apple and Onion from time to time. Gentle Giant: One of the biggest characters on the show, and also one of the most nicest. Riddle for the Ages: Just what exactly did he do to end up in prison in the first place?

characters.name: Patty
characters.description: Berserk Button: Whatever you do, don’t ever lie to her, or else she’ll punish you with Patty’s Law, as Falafel eventually found out. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Downplayed with the "Jerk" part. Although she is strict with Apple and Onion when it comes to managing the store, she ultimately means well and only acts as such to keep the store afloat. Jerkass Ball: She is more abrasive than usual in “One Hit Wonder,” where she makes the duo clean up by manually separating pieces of dirt on whether or not it’s “precious debris.”

characters.name: Pizza
characters.description: Nice Guy: He’s a very friendly and easygoing fellow towards both his customers and friends, Onion even lists this as one of the four reasons he thinks Pizza’s Diner is a good restaurant. Temporarily a Villain: In “Za,” Apple and Onion make various changes to his diner to make it more trendy and get recognized as a top food place. One of these changes are making himtake a level in jerkass, whichbackfires on the duo as he accepts the changes to the restaurant and refuses to turn it back once they realize that the changes made the restaurant worse for them.

characters.name: Hoagie
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: He plays a main role in the episode “Broccoli,” where Apple and Onion attempt to get him to fix their roof after Apple accidentally gives him all the money for the repairs, thus causing him to not bother working on their roof. Everyone Has Standards: Although he’s mostly aLazy Bumfor most of “Broccoli,” the moment he sees the news aboutApple and Onion’s (faked) deaths, he is genuinely put off by it and evenlaments on what he did wrongbefore leaving to go to their funeral. Hidden Depths: If Chicken Nugget's word is any indication, he's insanely good at making vegtable soup. Jerkass Has a Point: Sure, he slacked off by not fixing Apple and Onion's roof, but when he declares that he's not going to fix their roof after theyfaked their own deathsto get his attention, he somewhat has a point considering how said stunt scared him and would require a lot of professional therapy. Lazy Bum: After Apple gives him all of Falafel’s money now instead of splitting it into halves, he spends his time slacking off and buying things with his money than actually fixing the duo’s roof.

characters.name: Chicken Nugget
characters.description: Berserk Button: Aside from people breaking the law, making fun of his role as a police officer is another way to get him peeved. Catchphrase: “Hey! Haven’t you read the sign?!” The Comically Serious: He takes his job as a police officer very seriously, which puts him in contrast to Apple and Onion’s wacky antics earning them his ire. Hero Antagonist: In episodes involving him, he usually plays the role of the antagonist by preventing Apple and Onion from accessing something or doing a certain goal. However, he’s merely trying to uphold the law, as Apple and Onion’s methods of doing things are often illegal. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He may be no-nonsense and strict, but it’s all in the sake of keeping the law intact along with his job. It helps that he’s actually a decent person as long as he isn’t witnessing someone breaking the law (which is to say, pretty often).

characters.name: Jerk Chicken
characters.description: The Bad Guy Wins: He stands out as the only antagonist to actually best the duo in their own game, and in both of his appearances at that (though one of his victories was due to a flaw in the duo's revenge plan). Catchphrase: "Larda mercy!" Jerkass: He is quite the unpleasant fellow, considering the fact that he scams the duo out of free pizza, making their pizza delivery service run out of money, and making them buy his house which turns out to be falsely advertised in most of its aspects. Large Ham: One of the most bombastic characters in the show, no thanks to his rather expressive movements and his rather dramatic Jamican accent. Loophole Abuse: In his titular episode, he exploits a flawed coupon he obtains in order to get free pizza from Apple and Onion by stating that it doesn't have an expiry date, therefore making it able to be used infinitely, pulling off various tricks and traps to delay the duo in order to make them late to the 15 minute delivery timer, and building a house out of scraps in order to continue getting pizza since a scrap house does qualify as a home.

characters.name: Ice Cream
characters.description: Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Compared to his current design, his hat in his first episodes of appearance resembled a cherry more closely. Jerkass: Arguably the most unpleasant of the recurring background characters, since he is often rude towards others for no reason. Laser-Guided Karma: In “4 on 1,” he cracks a couple of rather insensitive remarks regarding Onion’s fear of crowds and tendency to freeze up. He eventually gets a basketball accidentally thrown at his face when Onion tries shootingwith some clothes wrapped over his head. Pet the Dog: As much of a jerk he can be at times, he does come to Apple and Onion’s funeral after their(fake)deaths and mourns their demise.

characters.name: Gingerbread Cookie
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: Even compared to the main duo themselves, he stands out as quite an oddball, especially with his whole rat king shtick. Crazy-Prepared: Apparently he has an entire system made to battle intruders in case they come to attack him, complete with a uniform for the occasion. He even calls his protocol “I Knew This Would Happen One Day.” Nice Guy: Despite being a rather strange self-titled “German Rat King,” he’s not that bad of a guy and is quite affable towards the duo. Pest Controller: He is capable of making his rats do various things for him, even being able to form a scooter to travel around in. Unwitting Instigator of Doom: In “Sausage and Sweetie Smash,” he offers Apple an entire mountain’s worth of sausages, unknowingly causing his sausage addiction to intensify to the point Apple becomes a sausage gremlin, thus kicking off the episode’s climax.

characters.name: Apple and Onion's Parents
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: Onion's Dad gets to play an important role in "Rotten Apple," coming over for a skiing trip with his son, but also having to deal with his suspicions towards Apple. Flat Character: Save for Onion's Dad, they don't have much of their personalities fleshed out aside from beingjust as polite as the duo. Nice Guy: Much like the duo themselves, they're polite and friendly to their sons and are willing to help them start a new life. No Name Given: None of them are given a name throughout the series' run. Small Role, Big Impact: While they only appear in the first episode and make minor appearances afterwards, they're responsible for the duo becoming best friends with each other and establishing the series' main setting.

characters.name: Lemon Drop
characters.description: Intergenerational Friendship: Despite Apple and Onion being full-grown adults in contrast to Lemon Drop’s young age, it doesn’t stop them from being on good terms with each other. Unwitting Instigator of Doom: She inadvertently causes (and becomes a part of) theChain of Harmin “Apple’s in Trouble” by messing up the duo’s money counting, unaware that they now have to work instead of goofing off. This results in her being scolded by Apple, which in turn causes her mood to sour and act unruly in school.

characters.name: Water
characters.description: Captain Obvious: He tends to point out the obvious regarding certain statements, usually when said statement is about him. Catchphrase: Though it’s more so a vocal sound than a phrase proper, he tends to make an “Ah-Ah-Oh!” sound whenever he beatboxes. Character Tic: Whenever he speaks, he tends to beatbox while making noises with his throat (or rather, the closest area nearby his mouth). He even does this while laughing. Flat Character: Like most of the minor background characters, his personality is made to be relatively simple, with most of his appearances revolving around his tendency to beatbox.

characters.name: Energy Bar
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: While she initially comes off as cordial, if a bit condescending towards the duo, it gets thrown out the window when she tries to outdo their bottle catch game by making her own brand of “bottle catch bottles” (which are actually regular bottles in a fancy shell) and marketing it as the original. Hypocritical Humor: She mocks Patty for being immature, despite instigating their brief teasing fight earlier. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: To Patty, since both of their stores are next to each other and often have argument on which one of them is more superior.

characters.name: ɘlqqA(Apple's Reflection)
characters.description: Allegorical Character: He is more or less the embodiment of Apple’s jealousy, being the motivator for Apple to get Cotton Candy out of the picture in order to be best friends with Onion again.Him parting ways with Apple after he admits he doesn’t need himself is symbolism for how he eventually gets over said jealousy and accepts that he’s (presumably) not Onion’s best friend anymore. Dark Reprise: "Apple & ɘlqqA", a darker version of the theme song, where they state they're number one and that they don't need Onion, ending with them saying "notwelcome" and the reflection letting out anEvil Laugh. Evil Counterpart: To Apple himself. Evil Sounds Deep: He has a much lower tone of voice compared to Apple to indicate him being a bad guy. Graceful Loser:After Apple accepts that he doesn’t need himself, he takes his loss pretty well to the point ofcongratulating himbefore peacefully parting ways.

characters.name: The Whalespotters
characters.description: Academia Elitism: They see themselves as more superior than “landlubbers” due to adapting to the sea’s environment. Onion even refers to them as “elitist snobheads” after leaving their group. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: While they are cordial with anyone who is just as knowledgeable about the sea like them, the same can’t be said for anyone who isn’t, as Apple and Onion later find out. Hate Sink: Compared to most of the other rude characters in the show, whose behavior was balanced by being equally as funny as they are obnoxious, the Whalespotters’Jerkassbehaviour isn’tPlayed for Laughsas much to emphasize the wedge driven between Onion and Apple’s friendship because of them.

characters.name: Kernel
characters.description: Berserk Button: Anything that has to do with either karaoke or singing is enough to rile him up, even if it’s just mentioned. Freudian Excuse: His generally abrasive demeanor and hatred of singing is due tobeing bullied by his own friends in a singing contest in 1st grade. Incredibly Lame Fun: The party he helps set up for Apple and Onion is nothing more than just sitting on chairs, with the games being a Rubix cube puzzle and a math quiz. The Napoleon: One of the shortest characters in the show, and also has quite the temper to boot. Opening-Up Moment: The moment he finally pops,he becomes much more calmer and admits that he became angry and grown to despise singing due to being bullied in a singing contest.

characters.name: Onion’s Voices
characters.description: Allegorical Character: They each represent a certain negative feeling, with the first voice being anxiety, the second voice being self-doubt, the third voice being low self-esteem, and the fourth voice representing panic. Character Tic: The third voice tends to flop his head and hands from side to side whenever he’s speaking, and the second voice always has his hands outstretched and furrows his unibrow whenever he talks. Graceful Loser:When Onion finally gets over his fear of crowds by looking deeper into his memory, the third voice says “Well, we had a good run.” in an accepting tone before all four of them fade away. Jerkass: The second and third voices are the most actively judgmental ones of the bunch and constantly tease Onion over his fear of crowds. Knight of Cerebus: While they aren’t outright evil and more so extremely judgmental, their interference with Onion’s confidence marks their episode of appearance,4 on 1, as one of the more emotional episodes in the series.
